text:
rachel: Hey team — ACME asked for a Private VPC sizing rec for their holiday promo (2-week peak). Need a conservative GPU-hours plan + burst strategy. They expect ~800 concurrent low-latency chat sessions, avg session 150 tokens, peak qps ~2200. Any quick ballpark?

kai: Ok, rough sketch: 800 concurrent * 150 tokens = 120k tokens in-flight. At 16k context typical -> latency-sensitive model needs KV-resident working set.

maria: For throughput -> translate to GPU hours: assume 1 A100-80GB can sustain ~1800 tok/s for our optimized runtime (single request stream). Peak 2200 qps ~ ~ (we should look at tok/s distribution).

tony: Quick calc I do in head: peak tokens/sec = 2200 qps * 150 tokens = 330k tok/s. If an A100 can do 1800 tok/s, naive pods = 330k/1800 ≈ 184 GPUs. That sounds huge because we used single-stream numbers. We should use batching and KV caching — effective tokens/sec per GPU jumps.

kai: Exactly — with continuous batching and 50% cache hit on prefixes we commonly reduce effective token load by ~40-60%. If we assume 2.5x effective efficiency from batching+cache, GPUs ~ 75.

maria: For Private sizing I'd recommend designing for 2 failure domains: N = baseline (75), plus 30% headroom = 98, round to 100 GPUs (A100-80GB equiv) for the peak window.

rachel: Nice. What about GPU-hours estimate across the 2-week promo? They want committed vs burst numbers for finance.

finance: We need a monthly GPU-hour estimate to surface cost. If 100 GPUs for 14 days non-stop = 100 * 24 * 14 = 33,600 GPU-hours. Add pre/post ramp ~20% -> ~40,320 GPU-hours.

ops-oncall: For burst policy, we can provision a small reserved pod (40 GPUs) + spot/backfill capacity up to 100. Plan: reserved 40, cold-start buffer of 2-3 hours for new pods, and an autoscaler with policies: scale aggressively on sustained queue > 2 min, scale conservative on short spikes.

maria: Also consider model variants: we can serve a quantized Q4_0 variant for best-efficiency during non-critical traffic — that reduces GPU need by ~30% but may impact quality. Suggest A/B fallback routing.

kai: Networking/region constraints: ACME wants EU-primary. We need enough rack-level NVLink fabric per pod. Recommend 8 GPUs per NVLink-enabled node for NVLink sharded KV workloads. So physical nodes = 100 GPUs / 8 = 13 nodes (round up 14). Account for spare node -> provision 16 nodes.

tony: Ops note: cooling and power headroom — 16 nodes with A100-style cards ~ 30kW. Confirm datacenter PDUs and CRAC capacity. If on customer premises, request rack power profile prior to procurement.

rachel: Any quick runbook lines we should give ACME? They want an ops checklist for go-live day.

ops-oncall: Runbook bullets: 1) Pre-warm KV cache with golden prompts 24h prior. 2) Validate autoscale hysteresis: test synthetic ramp to 1.2x expected. 3) Monitor token latency p50/p95, queue depth, GPU util, and NVLink errors. 4) Fallback route to quantized variant when p95 > 600ms or queue > 4000.

infra-bot: Deploy-preview: created draft sizing doc -> link: https://redwood.internal/sizing/1950502468 (internal).

maria: Next steps: I'll draft an itemized GPU-hour workbook (reserved vs spot) + 3 procurement options (reserved commit, reserved+burst, fully reserved). Will share by EOD.

rachel: Thanks — if we can get a line-item for finance & a 1-page ops checklist, I can forward to ACME this afternoon. :thumbsup:

kai: I'll add NVLink / rack sizing notes to the workbook and validate the 2x hot-spare assumption.

finance: One ask — include a best/worst case cost table with GPU-hour sensitivity +/- 25% and the impact of 30% quantization shift.

rachel: Great, let's sync in 30 for the quick handoff.
